input_references.role: Timestamped GPS points for each commute trajectory

metadata.goal: Summarize the commuting driving behavior of users from the supplied repeated travel trajectories.
metadata.category: Multi-user commuting route choice and convergence
metadata.dataset_description: A WorldTrace-style dataset of 120 commute trajectories from 12 users between Northgate Residential District and Harbor Business District. It provides trip-level route choice, direction, start and arrival times, distance and speed, plus linked timestamped trajectory points.

insight_list.insight: Although users repeatedly commute between Northgate Residential District and Harbor Business District in both directions, most retain one fixed route; only 25% ever switch between corridors for the same origin–destination pair.

plot.title: User-Level Route Consistency
plot.description: The left panel counts distinct corridors used per user; the right panel shows the three A–B corridor geometries.

insight_list.question: For users repeatedly commuting between the same two districts, how many retain one corridor and how many ever use an alternative?

insight_list.insight: Despite user-level route variation, a clear main corridor is used by most trips, and the full time intervals spent on it consistently remain within the 07:00–10:00 morning and 16:00–18:00 afternoon commuting periods.

plot.title: Main Corridor and Commuting Periods
plot.description: Main-corridor geometries are overlaid with the full start-to-arrival intervals of every main-corridor trip in the two commuting windows.

insight_list.question: Which corridor is used by most supplied trips, and within what full time intervals do users travel on that corridor?

insight_list.insight: Among the 25% of users who try alternatives, alternative-route use declines over repeated commutes; after the fifth commute, all of them use the main commuting corridor.

plot.title: Route Convergence over Repeated Commutes
plot.description: The left panel traces each route-varying user’s choices; the right panel aggregates alternative-corridor use by commute number.

insight_list.question: For users who tried alternative corridors, how does alternative-route use change as they repeat the commute?

insights: Although users repeatedly commute between Northgate Residential District and Harbor Business District in both directions, most retain one fixed route; only 25% ever switch between corridors for the same origin–destination pair.

Despite user-level route variation, a clear main corridor is used by most trips, and the full time intervals spent on it consistently remain within the 07:00–10:00 morning and 16:00–18:00 afternoon commuting periods.
Among the 25% of users who try alternatives, alternative-route use declines over repeated commutes; after the fifth commute, all of them use the main commuting corridor.
summary: Most users repeatedly drive the same corridor between the two commuting districts, while only three users initially explore alternatives. The main corridor dominates the supplied trips, with each complete traversal remaining in the morning or afternoon commuting windows. The users who explored alternatives converge to the main corridor after several repeated commutes.
